item.title: 230 喜欢的事但「没什么用」，还值得花时间吗？
item.description:
有些事明明做着挺开心，可一想到「这有什么用」，觉得似乎不值得花时间，该怎么办？

当一件事没有带来收入、进步或看得见的成果，那份已经发生的开心，可以成为我们为此花时间的理由吗？

当我们说「没用」，又在如何定义「有用」？

节目尾声中 00:14:22 「一个柚子的秋天」邀请你一起体验与觉察「无用之用」

一个柚子的秋天，

不只有金黄的脸，

第一次甜，第二次惊艳

一个柚子的秋天，

没有人规定它的终点，

世界比想象中更远，

如果有一天，你也被生活剥开

愿你还能，闪闪发亮地冒险

item.title: 229 一直被推着往前走，轮到自己选时却不知道想要什么，该怎么办？
item.description:
轮到自己选，为什么反而会不知所措？

以前读书、考试、找工作，每一步都有人告诉我该做什么，一直做得还不错。可现在，工作做了几年，继续做下去也行，换个方向也不是完全没可能。朋友问我，那你自己想要什么？我一下就答不上来了。我明明很会做决定，怎么轮到为自己选的时候，反而不知道该怎么选了？

回答这个提问，让人禁不住想再问出一个问题：你想不想OR允不允许你自己「长成自己的模样」？

今年夏天在瑞士 EGS 上学时，在阿尔卑斯山上拍了很多树的照片，回答这个提问的时候翻看这些照片，冒出一段小树枝和老树的对话，就这样慢慢长出一首回应这个提问十分精妙·美好的歌「长成自己的模样」，邀请心中有那个自己的模样的你，一起听听这期节目，尤其听听这首歌。

item.title: 227【Dialogue with Masters】Why is it so hard to truly change?
item.description:
英文播客

This is another deeply important episode of our EAT Masters series. In today's episode, we are joined by a pioneering leader in expressive arts therapy, Dr. Vivien Marcow Speiser, Professor Emerita at Lesley University in the United States, with five decades of international clinical practice, scholarship, and teaching experience. She joins us to explore a universal struggle we all carry:

Why is it so hard to truly change?

Vivien shares how the moments when life no longer makes sense may actually be the beginning of growth. She speaks about the cliffs we encounter in life, not as failures, but as deeply human turning points. In this conversation, she also guides us through a simple body and movement exploration, helping us sense how relationship, safety, conflict, and grounding already live inside the body, and how we might slowly learn to find our center and stand our ground.

Join us as we follow the thread of art to bind chaos into meaning.

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

In today's episode, I'm truly honored to be joined by a deeply respected leader in the field of expressive arts therapy, Dr. Vivien Marcow Speiser.

Vivien is Professor Emerita and co-director of the Institute for Arts and Health at Lesley University, and a distinguished research associate at the University of the Witwatersrand in South Africa. She is a licensed mental health counselor, a dance movement therapist, and an expressive arts therapist and educator. Across a lifetime of practice, teaching, and international collaboration, her work has taken her across the United States, Israel, and many parts of the world, developing and leading arts-based programs and working with individuals and communities navigating trauma, crisis, and cross-cultural conflict.

Her contributions extend not only through practice and teaching, but also through scholarship. She has served on the executive committee of ICAET, the International Association of Creative Arts in Education and Therapy, and is a co-editor of the CAET journal, contributing to the ongoing development of the field. She had received multiple Fulbright Senior Scholar Awards, and her work has been recognized internationally, including lifetime achievement honors in expressive arts and arts and health. Beyond her roles and recognitions, what feels especially meaningful in her work is a deep and ongoing commitment to using the arts as a way of communicating across borders, and of creating the conditions for both personal and social transformation.

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

「Expressive Arts Therapy — Conversations with Masters」

As a graduate of the first cohort of the China–U.S. Expressive Arts Therapy training program, I feel deeply honored to invite six leading figures in the field—senior practitioners, professors, and educators actively engaged in both clinical work and teaching—to join this series and share their insights.

They all graduated from Lesley University and bring decades of experience. They are not only experts, but also pioneers—people who have witnessed and shaped the field from its early beginnings to where it is today.

To make listening easier, this series will be released in two versions: a Chinese voiceover version and the original English audio. You can choose whichever feels right for you.

item.title: 226【大师解答系列】为什么真正的改变总是如此困难？| Vivien Marcow Speiser博士为你解答
item.description:
本期是【EAT大师解答系列】的第5期。本期邀请到表达性艺术治疗领域极具开创性的领军人物——美国 Lesley University 莱斯利大学荣休教授 Vivien Marcow Speiser 博士。她拥有超过五十年的国际临床实践、学术研究与教学经验。

这一次，她将和我们一起走进一个几乎每个人都会面对的生命提问：

【为什么真正的改变总是如此困难？为什么我们总会一次次回到同样的模式里？】

那些生命开始“不再有意义”的时刻，或许恰恰是成长真正开始的地方。Vivien谈到人生中那些仿佛“悬崖”般的时刻——它们并不只是失败，而是作为人的生命中，一个极其深刻的转折点。在这场对话中，她也会带领我们进行一段简单的身体与动作探索，让我们慢慢感受到：关系、安全感、冲突，以及那些关于连接与距离的经验，其实一直都活在我们的身体里；而在关系与变化之中，我们如何一点一点地重新找到自己的中心。

加入我们，一起顺着艺术的线索，将那些混乱与失序，慢慢编织出属于自己的意义。

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

今天这一期，我非常荣幸邀请到表达性艺术治疗领域一位备受尊敬的重要人物——Vivien Marcow Speiser 博士。Vivien 是美国 Lesley University 艺术与健康研究所的荣休教授与联合主任，同时也是南非金山大学（University of the Witwatersrand）的杰出研究员。她是一位持证心理咨询师、舞动治疗师，以及表达性艺术治疗师与教育者。

在超过半个世纪的实践、教学与国际合作生涯中，她的工作足迹遍及美国、以色列以及世界许多地区，长期致力于发展与带领艺术疗愈项目，并陪伴个人与社群穿越创伤、危机，以及跨文化冲突中的生命经验。

她的贡献不仅存在于临床与教学中，也深深延伸到了学术领域。她曾担任国际创造性艺术教育与治疗协会（IACAET）执行委员会成员，同时也是CAET的联合编辑之一，持续推动着整个表达性艺术治疗领域的发展。

她曾多次获得富布赖特高级学者奖，她的工作也在国际上获得广泛认可，包括表达性艺术以及艺术与健康领域的终身成就荣誉。但比起这些身份与荣誉，让人深深感触的是她始终持续地相信并践行着：让艺术成为不同人、不同文化之间彼此理解与连接的语言，并借由艺术，创造出能够促成个人与社会转化的空间与可能。

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

本期节目是我们的《艺术救心丸》将推出一个为期两个月的“表达性艺术EAT大师解答”系列，我十分荣幸邀请到6位全球表达性艺术领域的顶尖且资深的大师级、且在一线临床实践、教学的专家、教授为我们直接进行答疑解惑，TA们都毕业于表达性艺术治疗的学科原初发源地——美国莱斯利大学，都拥有几十年实践和教学经验，是这个学科从无到有、到稳步发展的前辈、亲历者。

item.title: 225【Dialogue with Masters】Why praise outside, doubt inside?
item.description:
英文播客

This is another essential episode of our “EAT Masters Series.” In today’s episode, we are joined by expressive arts therapy expert Kit Jenkins. Drawing on over thirty years of experience — spanning her long-standing faculty role at Lesley University and her transformative leadership as co-founder of the respected nonprofit RAW Artworks for young people — Kit joins us to explore a question that touches us all:

“I feel not good enough even when I'm praised. How can I truly start to validate myself from within?”

 When external praise fails to reach us, it’s often because a voice Kit calls “The Critic” has occupied our minds. We try to banish or erase it, but Kit reminds us that relationships don’t just exist between people—they live and breathe within our bodies.

In this episode, Kit will guide you through a profound imaginative journey to meet your inner critic face-to-face. But this journey requires more than just imagination; it requires the most important tool in a therapist’s toolbox: Presence. By shifting your internal ground and establishing a dialogue with this voice rather than being defined by it, allowing you to rediscover your own inner strength and peace.

Join us as we use creativity to move beyond verbal self-judgment and find the courage to stand in our own presence. 

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

In today’s episode, I’m truly honored to be joined by a senior expert in the field of Expressive Arts Therapy Kit Jenkins. Kit has been teaching as adjunct faculty at Lesley University for over 30 years, contributing to multiple graduate programs, including the expressive arts therapy master’s program. She has also taught at the European Graduate School in Switzerland and at Tufts University.

She is the founding Executive Director of RAW, a highly respected nonprofit organization, where she led its growth for over three decades and raised over $35 million in support of its mission.

Kit’s work spans expressive arts therapy, community arts, and social impact — from co-founding a community arts studio for children and adolescents, to supporting marginalized communities through nonprofit work. She was also among the early contributors to the International Expressive Arts Therapy Association, helping to shape the field in its early years.

Beyond her professional work, Kit is also a mother of twins, both now pursuing creative and nonprofit paths, and she lives a life deeply connected to movement and nature — spending much of her time in or on the water, swimming and rowing. This sense of rhythm, patience, and lived creativity continues to inform her work in a very human way.⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

item.title: 224【大师解答系列】为什么被夸奖时总觉得自己不够好，该如何真正从内在认可自己？| Kit Jenkins为你解答
item.description:
本期是【EAT大师解答系列】的第4期。本期邀请到表达性艺术治疗领域的专家 Kit Jenkins。她拥有三十多年的丰富经验——既包括在莱斯利大学长期担任教师的教学工作，也是备受尊敬的非营利组织 RAW Artworks 的联合创始人。今天，Kit 将和我们一起探讨一个几乎每个人都会遇到的问题：

【为什么被夸奖时总觉得自己不够好，该如何真正从内在开始认可自己？】

当外界的赞美无法真正被我们接住时，往往是因为有一个 Kit 称之为“内在批评者（The Critic）”的声音，占据了我们的内在空间。我们常常试图去消除它、压制它，但 Kit 提醒我们：关系并不只存在于人与人之间，它也活在我们的身体之中，与我们一起呼吸。在这一期节目中，Kit 会带领大家展开一段深刻的想象之旅，去真正“面对面”地遇见这个内在的批评者。但这段旅程不仅仅依赖想象，它更需要一种最重要的能力——也是治疗师最核心的工具之一：临在（Presence）回到当下/此刻。

当我们开始改变自己的“内在的位置”，不再被这个声音定义，而是与它建立一种对话关系时，我们也会逐渐重新连接到属于自己的内在力量与内在的平静。

加入我们，一起用创造力走出那些语言里的自我评判，与当下此刻的自己在一起。

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

今天的节目，我非常荣幸能邀请到来自表达性艺术治疗领域的资深专家 Kit Jenkins。Kit 在Lesley University 担任兼职教师已超过三十年，参与多个研究生项目的教学工作，其中包括表达性艺术治疗硕士项目。她也曾在European Graduate School（瑞士欧洲研究生院）以及Tufts University任教。她是非营利组织RAW的创始执行总监，在超过三十年的发展中，带领机构持续成长，并成功筹集了超过3500万美元的资金，用于支持其使命的推进。

Kit 的工作横跨表达性艺术治疗、社区艺术与社会影响领域——从共同创办面向儿童与青少年的社区艺术空间，到通过非营利工作支持边缘群体。她也是IEATA的早期贡献者之一，参与了这一领域在初期的发展与建设。

在专业工作之外，Kit 也是一位母亲，她的双胞胎孩子如今也分别走在与艺术和公益相关的道路上。她的生活与身体、自然有着深刻的连接——一周大部分时间都在水中或水上，游泳或与伙伴一起划船。这种节奏感、耐心与“活着的创造力”，也持续地以一种非常人性的方式滋养着她的工作。

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

item.title: 222【Dialogue with Masters】 Break free from parents’ control?
item.description:
英文播客

This is another essential episode of our “EAT Masters Series.” In today’s episode, we are joined by expressive arts therapy expert Dr. Yousef AlAjarma. Drawing from over thirty years of clinical experience—ranging from academic halls to trauma recovery in conflict zones—he joins us to explore a struggle that resonates across cultures:

How do I break free from emotional blackmail when my parents say, “It’s all for your own good”?

When guilt becomes an invisible chain used to control our choices, we often feel trapped in shame. But Yousef reminds us that relationships aren't just about the words we speak—they are lived and stored within our senses and our bodies.

In this episode, Yousef invites you to become “a fish swimming in the deep.” Through this gentle yet profound metaphor, he guides you beyond the maze of verbal conflict to discover: How have external messages shaped your “scales” on the outside？What does your “inner self” truly need from the waters around you?

Join us as we use creativity to build a shield of love—learning how to navigate the complex currents of family and find the freedom to swim your own path.

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

In today’s episode, I’m truly honored to be joined by Dr. Yousef AlAjarma, a professor in the Counseling Department at William James College, and a registered expressive arts therapist and licensed mental health counselor.

He brings years of experience working at the intersection of expressive arts, trauma, and community mental health, with a particular focus on resilience, family systems, and conflict transformation. Throughout his career, he has worked extensively with trauma survivors in Palestine, collaborating with organizations such as the United Nations, Doctors of the World, and the Palestinian Ministry of Education.

He’s former Executive Co-Chair of the International Expressive Arts Therapy Association, and continues to support individuals and communities through both clinical work and teaching.

item.title: 217【艺术救心丸】你会原谅那个权衡利弊后放弃你的人吗？
item.description:
本期提问：你会原谅那个权衡利弊后放弃你的人吗？

00:00 【艺术救心丸】大师解答系列介绍

“Letting go means ceasing to prescribe how things should go and instead observing how they actually go. ... It is the act of liberating the self from the tyranny of having to be in control of everything.

放手，不再规定事情应当如何发生，而是学会看见，它们本来正在如何发生。这是一种将自己，从“必须掌控一切”的执念中解放出来的能力。”

————————————

“When we stop repelling 'unwanted' emotions and instead allow them to exist and enter into the creation, they transform from 'tormentors' into 'guides.'

被排斥的情绪，会变成折磨；被允许的情绪，会开始说话。当它们进入你的表达，痛苦，也会生出指引的力量与方向。”

Trust the Process: An Artist's Guide to Letting Go, Shaun McNiff

————————————

【艺术救心丸】

  • 我们常常把自己当做需要被解决的问题，
  • 其实只是你的生命正在经历，
  • 欢迎收听《艺术救心丸》，
  • 用创造的方式表达，与真实的自己相遇。

每一期的“【艺术救心丸】，我们都会从一个提问出发，以一段表达性艺术治疗大师著作中的文字作为灵感起点，以体验至上&信任过程的底层信念，回应提问背后的情绪、感受与内在冲突，再邀请你进行一个日常可实践的表达性艺术的小小练习，没有标准，没有评判，只有你和你自己，待在一起。

它不是为了“找到正确或者对的答案”，而是让你在“说不清楚”的时刻，也能用另一种方式回应自己。让身体、感官和想象力参与进来，和你一起觉察、陪伴、流动、修复。

  • 欢迎你，和我一起，
  • 练习这一颗颗小小的艺术救心丸
  • 不把自己当做问题，
  • 跳出问题本身，从体验中，
  • 一点点靠近更真实的自己。
